prompt:
Photograph of a naval battle of the 1660s. On the left, a defeated ship
is a wreck: its masts are broken and fallen, its sails torn to rags and
burning, its hull shattered with gaping holes, listing heavily and half
under water, its stern sinking, with flames, thick black smoke and
floating wreckage, broken spars and barrels all around it; it is the
only thing burning. On the right, well apart from it, the victorious
galleon sails away untouched: its hull whole, its masts standing, its
sails full and clean in the wind, its flags flying, with no fire, no
smoke and no damage on it, under a clear patch of sky. The photograph is mounted in an ornate antique gilded wooden picture
frame that fills the whole image edge to edge, no wall around it. Style: one consistent look for the whole series, photographed like a
period film still of the 1660s Caribbean, natural warm light, gentle
film grain, muted rich colours with warm amber and deep teal tones,
moderate contrast, shallow depth of field, realistic textures, no text.
